Let \(t=\frac{s}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}\). The corrected equations are

\[
\frac{m}{2}t=4 \quad\Rightarrow\quad mt=8,
\]
\[
\left(1-\frac m2\right)t=7 \quad\Rightarrow\quad (2-m)t=14.
\]

From \(t=\frac8m\), substitute:

\[
(2-m)\frac8m=14
\]
\[
16-8m=14m
\]
\[
m=\frac{8}{11}.
\]

Then

\[
t=\frac{8}{8/11}=11.
\]

So

\[
\frac{s}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=11
\]
\[
s=11\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{8}{11}\right)^2}
=11\sqrt{\frac{185}{121}}
=\sqrt{185}.
\]

Thus the area is

\[
s^2=185.
\]

\[
\boxed{185}
\]
